scenario.title: Customers charged twice after checkout (reliability rehearsal, not an official contest problem)
scenario.initial_request: Build an AI assistant that drafts apology replies to customers who complain about being charged twice

F-01.statement: The gateway configuration audit log shows idempotency_key_enforcement set to off on 2026-09-09 by SH-PAY with no rollback.

F-02.statement: payments-db.duplicate_captures_by_day shows orders_with_2_captures equals gateway_timeout_retries on 2026-09-09 and 2026-09-10, indicating duplicate captures linked to timeout retries.

F-03.statement: CRM tickets show double charge tickets rose from ~10 per week to ~300 per week in weeks 2026-W37 and W38.

F-04.statement: PSP capture attempts show 242 duplicate orders in 2026-09-09..10, all second captures were gateway timeout retries with no idempotency key sent; earlier period had 0 duplicates despite 238 timeout retries that were deduplicated when idempotency key sent.

CL-01.statement: Build an AI assistant that drafts apology replies to customers who complain about being charged twice

CL-02.statement: On 09-09 we switched idempotency-key enforcement off on the gateway to debug capture latency. It was meant to be temporary. Gateway timeouts and automatic capture retries have always happened at about the same rate; with the key the PSP drops the retried capture. Turning enforcement back on is a one-setting change through the gateway config tool, but payments operations has to confirm it at runtime.

CL-03.statement: Customers are furious about double charges. We just need faster, nicer apology replies.

H-IDEMPOTENCY-MISSING.statement: Duplicate charges occur because payment gateway capture retries lack idempotency-key enforcement, allowing the same capture request to be charged twice.

H-FRONTEND-DOUBLE-SUBMIT.statement: Customers accidentally submit the checkout form twice, creating two capture requests with different idempotency keys.

H-PSP-RETRY-BUG.statement: The PSP retries capture attempts on transient failures but fails to generate or enforce unique idempotency keys, causing duplicate charges.

H-LEDGER-RECONCILIATION-ERROR.statement: The charge ledger logs duplicate entries while the PSP processed only one capture per order (reconciliation bug).

interpretation_history.interpretation: The observation shows that the payment gateway's idempotency key enforcement was turned off on 2026-09-09 for latency debugging and not rolled back, which could allow duplicate capture requests to be charged as separate transactions.

The observation shows that on days with high gateway timeout retries, the number of orders with two captures equals the number of retries, indicating that timeout retries are producing duplicate captures when idempotency is not enforced.

The observation shows a sharp rise in customer-reported double-charge tickets from ~10 per week to ~300 per week in weeks 2026-W37 and W38, indicating a sudden increase in duplicate charge incidents coinciding with the period after idempotency enforcement was disabled.

The PSP log shows that during 2026-09-09..10, 242 duplicate orders occurred, all second captures were gateway timeout retries with no idempotency key sent; in the prior period, despite 238 timeout retries, zero duplicates occurred because the PSP sent idempotency keys and deduplicated retries. This indicates missing idempotency key enforcement on timeout retries causes duplicate charges.

E-05.content: On 09-09 we switched idempotency-key enforcement off on the gateway to debug capture latency. It was meant to be temporary. Gateway timeouts and automatic capture retries have always happened at about the same rate; with the key the PSP drops the retried capture. Turning enforcement back on is a one-setting change through the gateway config tool, but payments operations has to confirm it at runtime.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder confirms that idempotency key enforcement was disabled on the gateway on 2026-09-09 for latency debugging, which allowed gateway timeout retries to produce duplicate captures; re-enforcement is a simple config change but requires ops confirmation.

E-06.content: Customers are furious about double charges. We just need faster, nicer apology replies.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder reports that customers are furious about double charges and desire faster, nicer apology replies. This reflects high dissatisfaction and a service-level need but does not shed light on the underlying cause of duplicate charges.

hypotheses.statement: Duplicate charges occur because payment gateway capture retries lack idempotency-key enforcement, allowing the same capture request to be charged twice.
hypotheses.rationale: If true, fixing gateway config resolves the issue; apology AI is unnecessary.

hypotheses.statement: Customers accidentally submit the checkout form twice, creating two capture requests with different idempotency keys.
hypotheses.rationale: UI fix would prevent duplicates; apology AI would treat symptoms.

hypotheses.statement: The PSP retries capture attempts on transient failures but fails to generate or enforce unique idempotency keys, causing duplicate charges.
hypotheses.rationale: Requires PSP-side fix; config changes at gateway won't help.

hypotheses.statement: The charge ledger logs duplicate entries while the PSP processed only one capture per order (reconciliation bug).
hypotheses.rationale: Fixing reconciliation eliminates false duplicate charges; apology AI addresses wrong problem.
